$comment: Checked-in tools/list manifest for the desktop MCP endpoint. Generated by scripts/gen-tool-manifest.ts — edit TOOLS there, not this file. See that script's header for why this is hand-written rather than auto-converted from the backend's zod schemas.

tools.name: get_editor_state
tools.description: Get the current editor state: active .pen file, user selection, top-level nodes, and available components. Call this first — Figma's metadata-first pattern.

include_schema.description: Whether to include the .pen file schema in the response. Set true if you need to understand the node format.

tabId.description: Route this call to a specific editor tab by id (see list_editor_tabs). Omit to target the currently focused tab.

tools.name: batch_get
tools.description: Retrieve nodes by id or search pattern, with depth control. Use to inspect structure before modifying.

type.description: Only return nodes with this type

name.description: Only return nodes whose name matches this regex pattern

parentId.description: Parent node ID to limit search scope

readDepth.description: How deep to read children (default 1). Nodes beyond this depth show as '...'.

searchDepth.description: How deep to search in the node tree. Unlimited if omitted.

resolveVariables.description: If true, variable references are resolved to their current values.

includePathGeometry.description: If true, include full SVG path geometry data.

tabId.description: Route this call to a specific editor tab by id (see list_editor_tabs). Omit to target the currently focused tab.

tools.name: snapshot_layout
tools.description: Get computed layout rectangles (positions/sizes after the layout engine runs). Key for design-to-code fidelity — use to check placement, overlap, and clipping.

parentId.description: Subtree root to inspect. Omit for the whole document.

maxDepth.description: Depth limit for traversal. Default is direct children only. Be careful with large values.

problemsOnly.description: If true, only return nodes with layout problems (clipping, overflow).

tabId.description: Route this call to a specific editor tab by id (see list_editor_tabs). Omit to target the currently focused tab.

tools.name: get_variables
tools.description: Read all design variables (tokens) and themes defined in the .pen file.

tabId.description: Route this call to a specific editor tab by id (see list_editor_tabs). Omit to target the currently focused tab.

tools.name: get_screenshot
tools.description: Take a screenshot of a node for visual verification — enabled only for MCP clients (not the built-in chat agent). Omit nodeId to screenshot the current selection (errors if none or more than one node is selected). Returns a PNG image.

nodeId.description: Node to screenshot. Omit to use the current selection.

tabId.description: Route this call to a specific editor tab by id (see list_editor_tabs). Omit to target the currently focused tab.

tools.name: batch_design
tools.description:
Execute batch operations on the .pen node tree. Accepts a mini-script string with operations:

**Operations:**
- `binding=I(parent, nodeData)` — Insert new node. Works both for a freshly-created parent binding AND for adding a child to an already-existing node: pass the existing node's id/path as `parent` (e.g. `I("existingFrameId", {...})` or `I(card+"/body", {...})`). This is the ONLY way to add children to an existing node — `U()` cannot add, remove, or reorder children.
- `binding=C(sourceId, parent, overrides)` — Copy node (`positionDirection`/`positionPadding` for placement)
- `U(path, updateData)` — Update properties (cannot change id, type, or children)
- `binding=R(path, newNodeData)` — Replace node entirely
- `M(nodeId, parent?, index?)` — Move node
- `D(nodeId)` — Delete node
- `G(nodeId, "ai"|"stock", prompt)` — Generate/find image and apply as fill to frame/rectangle

See the deployed pen-editor bundle's own tool description for the full rules/examples list (auto-layout wrap/gap, min/max sizing, fills/strokes/effects stacks, corner radius/smoothing, constraints, masks, lists, variable font axes, etc.) — this manifest carries a summary only; the executing bundle's copy is authoritative.

Call get_guidelines(topic: "design-system") first for auto-layout and component-usage rules.

operations.description: The batch-design mini-script to execute. Required (or one of the compatibility aliases below).

design.description: Compatibility alias for "operations", for models that occasionally emit the wrong key name.

script.description: Compatibility alias for "operations", for models that occasionally emit the wrong key name.

batch.description: Compatibility alias for "operations", for models that occasionally emit the wrong key name.

tabId.description: Route this call to a specific editor tab by id (see list_editor_tabs). Omit to target the currently focused tab.

tools.name: set_variables
tools.description: Add or update design variables and themes. Merges by default; replace=true overwrites all.

variables.description: Variable definitions, as an object keyed by variable name. Simplest form — a plain hex string per name: `{"--brand-primary": "#3b82f6", "--brand-bg": "#ffffff"}`. Full form — an object per name with `type` ("color" | "number" | "string", default "color") and `value`: `{"--radius-lg": {"type": "number", "value": "16"}}`. Per-theme values use `themeValues`: `{"--brand-bg": {"type": "color", "value": "#ffffff", "themeValues": {"dark": "#0b0b0b"}}}`. Names may be given with or without a leading `--`/`$`. Nested token groups (e.g. `{colors: {primary: {$type, $value}}}`) are also accepted.

replace.description: If true, replaces all existing variables. Default is merge.

tabId.description: Route this call to a specific editor tab by id (see list_editor_tabs). Omit to target the currently focused tab.

tools.name: read_comments
tools.description: Read canvas comment threads (feedback pins). Each thread carries an order number, resolved state, and — when anchored to a node — that node's id and name. Pass threadId for a single thread, or omit it to list all threads.

includeResolved.description: Whether to include resolved threads. Default false (only unresolved threads are returned).

threadId.description: If given, return only this thread instead of the full list.

tabId.description: Route this call to a specific editor tab by id (see list_editor_tabs). Omit to target the currently focused tab.

tools.name: reply_comment
tools.description: Append a reply to an existing comment thread, authored by you (the agent).

threadId.description: The id of the thread to reply to.

tabId.description: Route this call to a specific editor tab by id (see list_editor_tabs). Omit to target the currently focused tab.

tools.name: resolve_comment
tools.description: Mark a comment thread as resolved, after you've addressed what it asked for.

threadId.description: The id of the thread to resolve.

tabId.description: Route this call to a specific editor tab by id (see list_editor_tabs). Omit to target the currently focused tab.

tools.name: leave_comment
tools.description: Drop one or more comment pins authored by you (the agent), each starting a new thread. Pass a batch of 1-50 comments in one call. Each item needs nodeId (anchors to that node's center) or both x and y (a world-space canvas point). Returns the created thread numbers.

comments.description: Batch of comments to leave in this single call (1-50). Each item needs nodeId, or both x and y.

nodeId.description: Id of the node to anchor this comment to (pin defaults to the node's center). Omit if using x/y instead.

x.description: World-space canvas x coordinate for the pin. Required together with y when nodeId is omitted.

y.description: World-space canvas y coordinate for the pin. Required together with x when nodeId is omitted.

text.description: The comment body (non-empty). Be specific and actionable.

tabId.description: Route this call to a specific editor tab by id (see list_editor_tabs). Omit to target the currently focused tab.

tools.name: read_embed_html
tools.description: Read part of an existing embed node's HTML without pulling the whole document into context. `outline` (default) returns the tag structure with attributes intact and text/deep subtrees elided; `grep` returns lines matching a literal substring with surrounding context, for byte-exact anchors to feed edit_embed_html; `full` returns the entire HTML. Always read before editing.

nodeId.description: Id of the embed node to read.

mode.description: outline = elided structure, grep = matches for `pattern`, full = entire HTML.

pattern.description: Literal substring to search for (not a regex). Required when mode is 'grep'.

contextLines.description: Lines of context around each grep match.

maxDepth.description: Nesting depth kept in outline mode; deeper subtrees are summarized.

tabId.description: Route this call to a specific editor tab by id (see list_editor_tabs). Omit to target the currently focused tab.

tools.name: edit_embed_html
tools.description: Apply targeted text edits to an existing embed node's HTML instead of rewriting the whole screen. Each edit replaces an exact substring (oldString) with newString; an empty newString deletes the match. ALWAYS use this — never rewrite the whole htmlContent — when changing part of a screen that already exists: rewriting a whole screen costs thousands of tokens and silently drifts parts you weren't asked to touch. Read the fragment with read_embed_html first.

nodeId.description: Id of the embed node to edit.

edits.description: Edits applied in order, each against the result of the previous one.

oldString.description: Exact substring to find. Must occur exactly once unless replaceAll is true.

newString.description: Replacement text. An empty string deletes the matched fragment.

replaceAll.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match.

tabId.description: Route this call to a specific editor tab by id (see list_editor_tabs). Omit to target the currently focused tab.

tools.name: rename_layers
tools.description: Rename one or more layers (nodes) to logical, human-readable names in a single undoable step. Read each layer's type, text content, and hierarchy first (via get_editor_state / batch_get) so the names reflect each layer's role.

renames.description: One {id, name} entry per layer to rename.

tabId.description: Route this call to a specific editor tab by id (see list_editor_tabs). Omit to target the currently focused tab.

tools.name: find_empty_space_on_canvas
tools.description: Find available empty space on the canvas in a given direction with the specified dimensions. Use before inserting new top-level frames to avoid overlapping.

direction.description: Direction to search for empty space.

nodeId.description: Reference node to search around. Omit to search around entire canvas content.

tabId.description: Route this call to a specific editor tab by id (see list_editor_tabs). Omit to target the currently focused tab.

tools.name: get_guidelines
tools.description: Get design guidelines and rules for a topic (design-system, code, table, tailwind, landing-page).

tabId.description: Route this call to a specific editor tab by id (see list_editor_tabs). Omit to target the currently focused tab.

tools.name: get_style_guide_tags
tools.description: Get all available style guide tags. Call before get_style_guide to know which tags to use.

tabId.description: Route this call to a specific editor tab by id (see list_editor_tabs). Omit to target the currently focused tab.

tools.name: get_style_guide
tools.description: Get a style guide for design inspiration, by tags or by name.

tags.description: 5-10 tags to search for a matching style guide.

name.description: Specific style guide name to retrieve.

tabId.description: Route this call to a specific editor tab by id (see list_editor_tabs). Omit to target the currently focused tab.

tools.name: list_editor_tabs
tools.description: Desktop-only: list this app's open editor tabs, their titles, whether each is active/focused, and whether each is ready to receive MCP tool calls (mcpReady). Use to discover tabId values for explicit routing when more than one tab is open. This tool does not exist on pen-editor-backend's MCP surface — it is answered entirely by the desktop app, without involving any editor tab.
